摘要

  • Starting today, anyone in Dallas can download the Waymo app and hail a fully autonomous ride. Since opening our service in February, we’ve welcomed nearly 150,000 riders in Dallas from our interest list to experience the safety, reliability, and magic of Waymo, and now we’re offering our service to everyone.We’ve proudly helped Dallasites run errands, commute to work, and celebrate nights out with friends. Now, we’re going a step further to unlock a new way for tourists and other visitors to get around the city. We continue fully autonomous testing at Dallas Love Field Airport terminals and look forward to serving travelers there soon. And to get there efficiently, we’ll soon begin fully autonomous testing on Dallas freeways, which is the final step before offering these routes to public riders.The Dallas community has embraced Waymo as a vital resource for expanding accessible and reliable transportation options across the region. Chris Justl, CEO, Epilepsy Foundation Texas, shared, "Waymo autonomous vehicles are not just the future—they’re a transformational step forward for the epilepsy community and anyone living with medical conditions that limit their ability to drive, creating a new pathway to safe, independent travel. At Epilepsy Foundation Texas, we’re proud to partner with Waymo to help bring this future to life across Texas.”Rolling with Waymo in Dallas has never been easier. Simply download the Waymo app and ride today!

所发生的情况是，您的服务不足的巴士必须增加每个环路的停靠站才能生存。

在某些区域，离开死胡同区需要步行 15 至 20 分钟；所以你需要在该区域停留一两站。

现在您只需步行一小段路即可到达车站；但如果您希望这是一个可行的替代方案，则需要一定的服务频率。

这意味着路线需要在整个星期都活跃，而不仅仅是假设的高峰期（否则每个人都需要一辆车）。

那么，如何才能让每辆公交车的平均乘客人数达到较高水平呢？更多站点？

但如果每个站点都需要进出死胡同，则旅行时间就会增加。

最终人们不再忍受额外的时间，转而购买汽车。

所以你最终会遇到空巴士运行的情况……看起来比 Waymo 糟糕得多。

What happens, is your underserved bus has to increase stops per loop for viability.

You have areas where leaving the cul-de-sac zone takes 15-20 minutes on foot; so you need a stop or two in the zone.

Now you have a short walk to the stop; but if you want this to be a viable alternative, you need some frequency of service.

And that means that the routs need to be active across the whole week, not just the hypothetical peak (otherwise everyone needs a car anyway).

So how do you actually get a high average number of riders per bus? More stops?

But if each stop needs to go in and out of a cul-de-sac, the travel time goes up.

Eventually people stop tolerating the extra time, and get cars.

So you end up with a case of empty busses running... Seems much worse than a waymo.

并不是说要反驳你的观点，只是指出在德国等地，公交车运行得非常完美。那里的人们真的很自豪，你甚至可以乘坐公共交通工具去徒步旅行，公共汽车干净、安全、便宜（比开车便宜）。
Not saying to refute your point just flagging that in places like Germany the bus works flawlessly. People there are really proud that you can even go hiking with public transport, buses are clean, safe and cheap (cheaper than using your car).
